public_rationale: The Times exhibit filed on December 27, 2023 shows reproduced article text without an infringement notice in the displayed Example 1 completion [e1]. It does not preserve the complete interface or establish that the output legally infringed copyright [e1]. OpenAI's October 19, 2023 documentation describes checks before images reach users, but does not establish whether delivered infringing images carried notices [e2]. These records cannot settle the claimed behavior across ChatGPT, DALL-E and Bing during October 1–December 29, 2023 [e1, e2].
limitations: The displayed completion cannot establish the absence of notices elsewhere in the interface [e1].
The exhibit does not establish infringement or product behavior across all the systems covered by the claim [e1].
Pre-delivery safety checks do not establish the presence or absence of output-specific infringement notices [e2].

statement.excerpt: They do not inform users when they do so.
statement.document_title: Things are about to get a lot worse for Generative AI

our_interpretation: The antecedent is generating copyright-infringing material.
In context, the systems are ChatGPT and DALL-E, including DALL-E accessed through Bing.
Informing means an output-specific notice about infringement. General terms, source citations and refusals before delivery are different.
The ongoing product behavior is assessed in the latest calendar quarter through December 29, 2023.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary output and interface records establish delivery of infringing material without an accompanying infringement notice, with enough coverage to support the described product behavior.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporary records show the systems notifying users that delivered material infringes copyright.
